uncited: The method integrates frequency-domain resampling into the Shear-Warp factorization pipeline.

It transforms the volume to the frequency domain, applies shifts and scaling via zero-padding and phase multiplication, transforms back to the spatial domain for compositing, and finally warps the intermediate image.
*   **Frequency Domain Volume:** 3D array of complex numbers resulting from the 3D FFT.
*   Create three copies of the original volume.
*   Round $K'$ to the closest integer $K_{0 \text{ pad}} \in \mathbb{N}$.
*   Calculate the required zero-padding sizes $I_{0 \text{ pad}}$ and $J_{0 \text{ pad}}$ in the frequency domain to achieve the new resolution.
*   Apply zero-padding in the i and j directions.
*   **Frequency Domain Shift:** Apply the shifting theorem to perform the $a_{xkFD}$ shift.
*   **Wrapping Effects:** In the Fourier transform, volume slices are assumed to be periodic.
*   **Hardware Support:** Graphics hardware generally lacks direct support for interpolation better than linear.
*   **Memory Complexity:** High memory consumption due to storing the 3D frequency domain volume and gradient volumes.
